hook.what_happens: A model stares at the camera while a graphic overlay prompts the viewer to think of their best photo.
hook.why_it_works: Engages personal vanity and self-image immediately.

narrative_arc: Prompt the viewer to visualize their best photo.
Introduce the common belief that our best photos are vastly superior.
Debunk this belief using statistical data from the Aella study.
Apply the data to a real-world case study of a professional model.
Relate the findings back to the viewer's personal life using UGC examples.
Call to action to visit the brand's website for self-improvement.

transcript.text: Let's do an experiment. Think of the best picture of yourself that you've ever taken.
Your 'this is her' photo. How much better is that photo than the average photo of yourself?
If you're like most people, you probably think it's notably better.
Aella's research indicates that on average, people think they look 17% better in their best photo than in their average photo.
But to other people, it turns out, they only look 5% better.
And in fact, 1 in 3 people actually have it backwards.
That is, other people prefer their average photo to the photo that they think is their best photo.
This might seem surprising, but look at this photo of Bhavitha Mandava.
She might think that this is a 'bad photo' of herself, as it's pretty casual and she has done tons of more glamorous shoots.
And it's her own face, so naturally she's more sensitive to contextual differences.
But as outsiders, we can see she's exceptionally beautiful in any photo.
This specific photo really doesn't make as much of a difference.
And the same is true about you. You would think, 'Oh, I look so different from photo to photo,' but you probably look pretty good regardless.
In fact, ask your boyfriend or girlfriend or friend to send you their favorite photo of you, and we can almost guarantee you'll be surprised at their choice.
If you want to glow up, click the link in bio at qoves.com.

cta.what: Visit Qoves.com via the link in bio to 'glow up'.

what_makes_it_work: Leverages scientific data to validate a highly relatable social insecurity.
Uses a professional model to objectively prove that 'average' photos still look great to outsiders.
Maintains a clean, high-end aesthetic that aligns with clinical self-improvement branding.
